title: Head and shoulders
desc: Three peaks and a neckline: wait for the close through it

cards.title: Three peaks
cards.situation: After a long rise, price makes three peaks: $50, $56, then $51. The lows between them both sit near $46. What’s forming?

chart.label: Three peaks at $50, $56 and $51 above lows near $46

options.feedback: A right shoulder below the head shows buyers getting weaker. The $46 neckline decides it.

options.text: A new uptrend: the middle peak is highest
options.feedback: The last peak failed below the middle one. That’s a head and shoulders forming, and $46 is the line to watch.
A double bottom is two lows at the same level after a fall. Here, after a long rise, three peaks sit above a $46 floor.

cards.title: Head, shoulders, neckline
cards.text: Three peaks: a **left shoulder**, a higher **head**, and a lower **right shoulder**. The **[[neckline|neckline]]** joins the two lows between them.

chart.label: Left shoulder, higher head, lower right shoulder, and the neckline under them

blocks.tip: Flip it upside down at the end of a fall and it’s an inverse head and shoulders: a possible turn up.

cards.title: Wait for the break
cards.text: The pattern counts only when price closes below the neckline. Sometimes it climbs back to test it from below.

chart.label: Price closes below the neckline, climbs back to test it from below, then falls

cards.foot: Old floor, new ceiling: the same idea as [[support|support]] turning into [[resistance|resistance]].

cards.title: Patterns fail often
cards.text: Many head and shoulders never break the neckline. Some break, then snap back. Selling on the shape alone gets beginners hurt.

chart.label: A head and shoulders shape that never breaks the neckline and rises instead

cards.rule: wait for a close below the neckline, and always use a stop.

cards.title: Where’s the trigger?
cards.q: Left shoulder $30, head $35, right shoulder $31. The neckline sits at $27. When is the pattern confirmed?

options.text: When the right shoulder forms at $31
options.feedback: A right shoulder is only a hint. Until price closes below the $27 neckline, nothing is confirmed.
The close below the $27 neckline confirms it. Until then, the three peaks are only a shape.
A return to the $35 head would mean buyers are back. That cancels the pattern; it doesn’t confirm it.
Right after the head, the right shoulder hasn’t even formed. Nothing counts until a close below the $27 neckline.

cards.title: It bounced
cards.q: A head and shoulders formed. Price touched the neckline, bounced, and rose above the right shoulder. What now?

options.text: Sell anyway: the shape is there
options.feedback: The shape was there, but the neckline held. No break means the pattern failed, so there’s nothing to act on.

options.text: The pattern failed: no break, no signal
options.feedback: The neckline held and price climbed back over the right shoulder. No break, no signal: the pattern failed.
Nothing is guaranteed. A failed top only means this pattern gave no signal.
Moving the neckline to fit is forcing it. The neckline held, so the pattern failed.

cards.headline: You can wait for the break.
lines: Three peaks: shoulder, higher head, lower shoulder.
The neckline joins the lows. Wait for a close through it.
Patterns fail often: always keep a stop.
